messages.subject: Issues with efaUnrotate() and oblqRotate() after updating to lavaan_0.6
parts:
Hi all,

I am doing some EFA using lavaan and semTools and got into a few hurdles after updating to lavaan_0.6. I found the same issues using two different semTools versions. (Because output is a bit long, I will use '====' to separate them.

I apologize if this is a wrong inference (I am a 100% newbie in R package programming) but it seems to me that there is a 'broken link' in  how semTools EFA functions access and extract information from the lavaan output object -- perhaps due to changes in how lavaan works now?


If I roll back to lavaan_0.5-22 and semTools_0.4-14, everything works perfectly.

parts:
2) Using lavaan_0.6-1.1144 and semTools_0.4-15.910:

In this case, summary(output) does not show the factor loadings.

You mean oblqRotate() does not?  It works fine using the example on the ?oblqRotate help page, using the same lavaan and semTools versions you are using above.  I can't deduce what the problem is because your output contains estimates of 2 factors, whereas your efaUnrotate(..., nf = 1) call only requests a single factor.  What are you leaving out?  It would help to store results of different models in different objects, so that you don't mistake an old "output" for the output you intend to inspect/rotate.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Hi Terrence,

I apologize for an editing mistake causing confusion: `efaUnrotate(..., nf = 1)` should be read as `efaUnrotate(..., nf = 2)` (in the copy-and-paste + editing before posting, I just messed it up. BOTH models reported are two-factor models).


As you can see in the second example: output for efaUnrotate displays results for a two-factor model; oblqRotate() is also about a two-factor model (as the column headers 'factor1', 'factor2' indicate).

Summarizing: 
- in the first example, efaUnrotate() works but oblqRotate() does not.
- in the second example, efaUnrotate() does *not* work: all reported factor loadings are zero. 



I will re-run the EFA again later and will report full outputs.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Issues with efaUnrotate() and oblqRotate() after updating to lavaan_0.6
parts: - in the second example, efaUnrotate() does *not* work: all reported factor loadings are zero.

OK, I didn't notice that before.  Thanks for specifically saying they were zero this time.  In that case, there was nothing wrong with the oblqRotate() function.  It only prints substantial loadings (I think > 0.3), and as you saw in the summary of the unrotated lavaan object, none of the loadings were large.  

So the problem was that all estimated loadings were zero.  I tried using your same arguments with example data from semTools and found the same result:

unrotated <- efaUnrotate(datCat[paste0("u", 1:8)], nf = 2, ordered = paste0("u", 1:8), estimator = "ULSMV")
summary(unrotated)
oblqRotate(unrotated)

The efaUnrotate() function asks lavaan for its starting values before fitting the model, but I needed to tweak the way they were stored.  It is fixed in the new development version of semTools (0.4-15.911), which requires R 3.4, so make sure the latest R is installed before installing semTools again:

devtools::install_github("simsem/semTools/semTools")

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
